body.objective: Replace the finite point-mode Rt-dressed positive scalar source by three compact continuum wave packets away from zero momentum, construct a common closable Gaussian image domain for the smeared pulled creators and finite-rank detector effects, and prove convergence of finite-volume packet approximants without promoting the result to general Eq. 19 or a packet scattering rate.
activates: a compact continuum dressed scalar source
a common closable packet creator/effect domain
finite-volume independence of the source and fixed-strength detector effect
body.current_gate: Use three normalized compact packet profiles on mutually disjoint and non-antipodal supports with epsilon <= |p| <= M. Rewrite the scalar pulled creators in normalized Jordan oscillators, prove the energy multipliers are bounded, retain the Gaussian squeezed vacuum and Laurent orbit, reconstruct the exact positive ghost-even packet frame, and prove L2 packet approximation implies vector and finite-rank effect convergence.
body.stop_condition: Land a certificate and method-distinct verifier for the packet cross Gram, positive frame, closability, packet-continuity estimates and finite-volume approximation theorem, while keeping the packet Hamiltonian strength, infrared removal, standard P_chi, general Eq. 19, global scattering and gravity explicitly open.
body.forbid: no delta-normalized momentum eigenstate called a packet; no use of E^-1 without a positive support gap; no omission of antipodal contraction conditions; no closable core called a bounded global Rt; no fixed-zeta effect called a dynamically integrated packet rate; no ordinary-Fock infrared, Eq. 19, gravity, BRST or LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL promotion
body.resource_hint: Normalize a1,a2 by a_r=(2E)^(3/2) A_r. Then d_Upsilon^dagger(f)=Z^-1 A1^dagger(2Ef), while on the pulled vacuum d_Omega^dagger(f)=Z[A2^dagger(f/(2E))-it A1^dagger(f)]. The full operator also has a reflected annihilator term; disjointness of K_i from -K_j removes its contractions in the declared three-packet frame. Use the standard number-operator creation bounds and the analytic Gaussian moments supplied by sup|z|<1 and sum|z|^2<infinity. Finite-rank Krein effects are Hilbert trace-class because J is bounded.
